Could mathematical notation itself be engineered to be more transformer‑native?

I’m exploring whether there exists a representation of mathematical reasoning that small language models can learn far more easily than raw Lean syntax — a kind of “low‑entropy math language” optimized for transformer inductive biases.

Lean 4 feels like the right place to search for this. It already encodes mathematics as typed DAGs, and its kernel gives us a perfect ground‑truth validator. That means we can safely build an experimental layer on top of Lean that tries out alternative, more explicit representations of the same underlying structures — and measure which ones small models learn most predictably.

The motivation is simple: instead of scaling compute endlessly, maybe we can make the representation easier for a small model to learn, so even an SLM can solve problems that currently require much larger models.

I’m working toward a small controlled experiment to test this idea, but I’d love to hear whether others have explored transformer‑native mathematical representations in Lean, or whether there are reasons this framing doesn’t apply the way I think it might.
